subject: Need help with an error in two.b.pls.

messages.author: f98fc9da3dc4715b
messages.subject: Need help with an error in two.b.pls.
parts:
Hi everyone,


My name is Eddie Gadee, I attended the PR Statistics Geomorph workshop in Wales this past month, and I was wondering if I can get some help or clarification on a small error I am receiving in a Geomorph command. I'm currently trying to conduct a two.b.pls command on some GPA-aligned arrays.

 

My work, in detail, is as follows: I have 6 specimens/.ply files of a certain bone found in a bird species I am investigating. For each specimen, I am digitizing 3 sets of landmarks. One set is the superior region of the bone (abbreviated as cg), one set is the midsection (bh), and the third set is the inferior portion of the bone (pc). I've digitized 6 landmarks for each specimen's cg part, 12 for each specimen's bh, and 10 for each pc. Now that I have .nts files for all of the landmarks I placed, I sorted them into 3 folders respectively (cg, bh, pc) and each folder contains a uniform 6 files/specimens.

 

I then created respective filelists for the files in each of the folders (cg.data, bh.data, pc.data), read them into R, and successfully performed gpagen on all 3 of the filelists. Now I want to perform a two.b.pls on all 3 arrays (which I am aware is possible and calls for other functions to be performed later on that I can do). Doing this for 3 arrays warrants this command being done between all 3 arrays anyway (cg,bh; cg,pc; bh,pc). The only problem is, when I enter my code as follows, I get this error:

 

> two.b.pls(cg.data[,,1], pc.data[,,1], iter=999)
Error in two.b.pls(cg.data[, , 1], pc.data[, , 1], iter = 999) : 
  Data matrices have different numbers of specimens.

While the error message sounds pretty straightforward, I am nonetheless confused because each one of my arrays do indeed contain a uniform amount of 6 specimens, and I don't understand what I am supposed to diagnose here. I verified that the amount of specimens are the same. The only thing I can guess is that by specimens, R is referring to landmarks? Could it be that R is telling me that each of my arrays need to have specimens that have the same number of landmarks, and not have one array of 6-landmarked specimens, one array of 12-landmarked specimens, and one of 10-landmarked specimens? This would mean I have to redigitize, which is time-consuming but okay, but I just want to confirm if my hunch is on the right track or if this is an error that I am not really understanding entirely. Any solution to being able to resolve this error and perform this command would be really helpful.

 

Thank you very much!

 

- Eddie

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Need help with an error in two.b.pls.
parts:
Hi Eddie,

the error message is meant to transmit exactly what you are interpreting, a different number of specimens. If dim(cg.data) and dim(pc.data) give you the same third element (i.e. the number of specimens) you should be OK.

Note however, that in your code you are passing to the function an index of the first specimen of each dataset (through [,,1]) which means that you are trying to run a pls with only one specimen. This is not possible, and it might be triggering the error you are seeing. Try to remove that and see if the function now works.

Hope this helps

Antigoni

parts:
Hi Antigoni,

Thanks for reaching out. When I remove the [,,1] from the code, this is the error I get:

> two.b.pls(cg.data, pc.data, iter=999)
Error in y[rownames(x), ] : subscript out of bounds

This is actually the code I tried initially, and I only added the [,,1] on my own after seeing this error and wondering if this would fix the error. The reason I tried this is because the first two dimensions of my data appeared as "null" when I entered dimnames, but even so, the third dimension of both sets have the same number of specimens:

> dimnames(cg.data)
[[1]]
NULL

[[2]]
NULL

[[3]]
[1] "CHLOROSTEJ162Landcg" "HEMPARV162Landcg"    "hemVir179413Landcg"

> dimnames(pc.data)
[[1]]
NULL

[[2]]
NULL

[[3]]
[1] "CHLOROSTEJ162Landpc" "HEMPARV162Landpc"    "hemVir179413Landpc" 
[4] "LCAER148Landpc"      "palmDolLandpc"       "VESTCOC146Landpc"

Hopefully this information is useful.

-Eddie
